title: Europe’s next budget fight – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR podcast on the fight over the EU's 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework, split between cohesion/farm-protecting 'friends of cohesion' and Germany-led 'frugals', with an Irish presidency compromise cutting the Commission's roughly EUR 2 trillion proposal by about 8%.

insights.claim: The EU's 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework talks have split member states into 'friends of cohesion', who want to protect money for poorer regions and farmers, and 'frugals', net contributors led by Germany who want a smaller budget focused on defence and competitiveness.
insights.speaker: Pierre Heilbronn, Mark Leonard, Guntram Wolff
insights.so_what: Budget priorities (defence and competitiveness versus cohesion and farm subsidies) determine which EU-funded sectors gain or lose in 2028-2034.
insights.locator: Every seven years, EU member states agree on the MFF

insights.claim: The Irish presidency's October 10th compromise would cut the Commission's almost EUR 2 trillion MFF proposal by about 8%, at the expense of competitiveness, foreign aid and emergency funds, while leaving farmer subsidies and cohesion funds untouched.
insights.speaker: Pierre Heilbronn, Mark Leonard, Guntram Wolff
insights.so_what: The cuts fall on competitiveness and external aid lines, so EU-level competitiveness and defence-adjacent funding is at risk while legacy farm and cohesion spending is protected.
insights.locator: On October 10th, the Irish presidency tabled a compromise

insights.claim: MFF negotiations are expected to reach a decisive phase in the weeks after the October 15th-16th Brussels leaders' meeting.
insights.speaker: Pierre Heilbronn, Mark Leonard, Guntram Wolff
insights.so_what: Watch the coming weeks for a deal or breakdown that sets the 2028-2034 EU spending envelope.
insights.locator: EU leaders are now meeting in Brussels on October 15th-16th

source_meta.author: Pierre Heilbronn, Mark Leonard, Guntram Wolff
